title: Turkey Chili
description: By Pierre Franey: You might not think of chili as an easy weeknight dish, but this turkey version from Pierre Franey will change your mind. It's fabulous, it's healthy and it can be cooked in about a half hour. A combination of dark and white meat really adds depth and richness of flavor, so try to find a mix, but all white meat (or a mixture of ground beef and turkey) will yield a stellar batch too.
ingredients: 1 pound ground turkey, white and dark meat combined
1 large sweet red pepper, cored, deveined and coarsely chopped
1 jalapeño, cored, deveined and finely chopped
1 tablespoon fresh oregano, chopped, or ½ tablespoon dried
1-2 cups canned diced tomatoes (1 regular can)
1 cup chicken broth, fresh or canned
1 (15-ounce) cans beans, cannellini or red kidney, if not drained, use slightly less broth
directions: Heat the oil over high in a large heavy pot and add the onions. Cook until lightly browned, about 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.

Add the turkey meat, garlic, sweet pepper, celery, jalapeño, oregano, bay leaves, chili powder and cumin. Stir to blend well, chopping down and stirring with the side of a heavy kitchen spoon to break up any lumps of meat. Cook for 5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, chicken broth, salt and pepper to taste. Bring to a boil, reduce heat and simmer, stirring occasionally, for 15 minutes.
Add the drained beans and cook, stirring occasionally, for 10 minutes longer. Serve in bowls with Cheddar, and sour cream and lime wedges, if desired.
